_comment: Seed material for L4, the creative engine (src/loops/creative.ts). This is the ONLY place the creative loop learns what VedicHour actually does, who it talks to, and what it may never say. Edit freely — read fresh on every run, no restart needed.
valueProp: VedicHour scores all 18 planetary hours (horas) of a given day against YOUR birth chart, and tells you which windows run clearer and which run heavier — for a specific kind of task (a negotiation, a first meeting, focused study, publishing something). Computed from real astronomical data — the same math a careful astrologer uses — and explained in plain English. It is a timing grid for your day, not a mood forecast for your star sign.
audience: Urban Indians aged 24-40 (Bengaluru / Delhi NCR / Mumbai / Pune / Hyderabad) plus the diaspora (US, UK, UAE, Singapore, Australia). Phone-first, scroll-fast, sceptical-but-curious. Many grew up around Jyotish at home and take it semi-seriously; they will instantly cringe at anything that sounds like a WhatsApp-forward astrologer, a doom prophecy, or a get-rich promise.
register: HINGLISH written in ROMAN / LATIN letters ONLY. Natural code-switching, the way people actually text: 'kal 11 baje meeting rakhun ya 4 baje?'. Never Devanagari or any non-Latin script — the downstream text-to-video and caption models reject non-Latin input.

families.weight: most ideas should come from here
families.brief: A specific, named, ordinary moment where a real person is choosing WHEN to do something. The whole idea is the moment, not the astrology. Concrete beats abstract every single time. BIAS TOWARD WEIGHT: the questions this audience actually asks in public are about relationships, marriage, and career turning points — reconciliation, 'when will my relationship start', 'any big career breakthroughs coming', whether to leave a job, whether to move abroad. Nobody loses sleep over when to schedule a meeting. Write the high-stakes MOMENT and keep the low-stakes CLAIM: we say WHEN to have the conversation, never what the other person will do.

families.brief: Contrast the EFFORT and TIME of getting a personal timing read the old way (finding a good astrologer, coordinating a sitting, waiting days for a written reply, going back for follow-ups) against roughly 90 seconds here, on your phone, on your own chart.
families.hardConstraint: NEVER state, imply, or hint at any rupee or dollar figure, discount comparison, or 'cheaper than X' claim — we cannot defend a price claim about anyone else. Compare TIME and EFFORT only.

families.brief: A sun-sign horoscope column is written for one-twelfth of the planet; your birth chart is not. Same date, same city, two different charts, two different days. Position VedicHour as the specific version of something the viewer already half-believes.
families.hardConstraint: Respect the tradition and everyone in it. Never mock Jyotish, never mock astrologers, never name or knock a competitor app, never call believers gullible. The enemy is the GENERIC, never the practice.

shotKinds.presenter: a real person on camera, talking to the phone. Give the video model a subject, an action, a camera move, lighting and mood.
shotKinds.broll: no dialogue, atmosphere or metaphor. Give the video model a subject, an action, a camera move, lighting and mood.
shotKinds.screencap: a real screen recording of the live product. The prompt is simply WHAT TO CAPTURE, pulled from screencapLibrary — no cinematography, because it is a recording, not a generation.

hardRules: Latin script only, everywhere — hook, script, captions, CTA.
No guarantees, no '100%', no 'miracle', no 'will definitely'.
Never 'the best hour' or 'the worst hour' as fact — VedicHour says 'clearer' and 'heavier' windows.
No health, money, legal, or relationship outcome promises. Not 'you'll get the raise' — instead 'you'll know which window runs clearer for asking'.
No fear-mongering, no doom, no curses, no 'bad luck'.
No invented social proof — no fake testimonials, no made-up user counts, no star ratings.
No competitor names and no mocking of astrology or astrologers.
No rupee or dollar figures of any kind.
Hook text must be readable in under one second — about 8 words maximum.

Write the moment people actually lose sleep over (a relationship, a family conversation, a career turn) but keep the claim small: WHEN to have the conversation, never what the other person will do. No 'will he come back', no reassurance, no prediction.
Shot 1 is always a presenter COLD OPEN of 3 seconds or less — he is already mid-answer, no greeting and no setup — and shot 2 is always the real product, so proof is on screen before second three.

Mid-thought is not the same as empty. The cold open must be a COMPLETE sentence a total stranger understands on its own, with the actual subject named in it — never 'isi baat pe atka hoon' (stuck on WHICH thing?), never a 'POV:' or 'Shayad' opener.

The first product shot is an INSERT: 2 seconds or less, wordless, cut inside his sentence. The product HOLD — 3 to 4 seconds where the screen is the payoff — always comes later. A long product screen at second three is an ad pivot, and it is what killed the last four batches.
At least two presenter shots must run BACK TO BACK, in different shot sizes, with no product screen between them. Face/screen/face/screen the whole way through is a metronome, not a reel.
The closing line lands on the thing the cold open opened, and carries vedichour.com inside it. A closing line that would fit on the end of any other reel we have written is a failed closing line.

Never render a figure of speech as an object. If the copy says window, door, green light, clock or crossroads, the picture shows the actual subject — the person deciding, the moment, or the real report — never the metaphor as a prop.
At most one b-roll shot per reel, and prefer none. A face cut against the real product screen is what a funded company's ad looks like; generic atmosphere footage is what cheap looks like.

No engine or astrology jargon in ad copy — never Swiss Ephemeris, Lahiri, ayanamsa, sidereal, whole-sign or vimshottari. If credibility is needed, say 'real astronomical data, the same math a careful astrologer uses'.

There is NO NARRATOR. Every word in the reel is said by the presenter on camera; screencap and b-roll shots carry no line at all. A music bed runs unbroken under the whole reel, so a wordless product beat is a cut, not dead air — and every narration line this brief ever produced turned out to be a product feature in a Hindi coat.
Screencap shots show the REPORT and its hour-slots. Never the pricing page, checkout, payment or onboarding.
